senses.definition: The hard outer covering of a bird’s egg, or a piece of that covering.
senses.example: I fished a tiny piece of eggshell out of the mixing bowl.

senses.definition: To push or send something out of its place.
senses.example: We pressed the button to eject the disk.

senses.definition: To order a person to leave an event or place.
senses.example: The referee can eject a player who keeps breaking the rules.

senses.definition: Able to stretch and then return to its earlier shape.
senses.example: The elastic strap stretches to fit a larger box.

senses.definition: Stretchy material used in bands or fabric.
senses.example: The elastic in my mask had worn out.

senses.definition: Enough space to move and work comfortably.
senses.example: Scoot the chairs apart so we each have some elbow room.

senses.definition: Older, especially when comparing family members.
senses.example: My elder brother is three years older than I am.

senses.definition: An older person, especially someone respected for their experience.
senses.example: The community’s elders shared stories about the old meeting place.

senses.definition: A vote held to choose people for particular roles, often in a government or group.
senses.example: Our class held an election for two student representatives.

senses.definition: Graceful and attractive.
senses.example: The bridge had an elegant curve.

senses.definition: Solving a problem clearly and simply.
senses.example: Dividing the beads into threes was an elegant way to check the total.

senses.definition: A school for children in the early years of formal education.
senses.example: My elementary school has a library next to the gym.

senses.definition: To remove something or decide it no longer belongs among the choices.
senses.example: We eliminated the green lid because it did not fit any of the jars.

senses.definition: To knock a player or team out of a contest.
senses.example: The last round eliminated two teams.

senses.definition: A kind of tree with leaves whose edges usually have small teeth.
senses.example: We rested in the wide shade of the elm.

senses.definition: Other or in addition to what has already been mentioned.
senses.example: What else should we bring for the picnic?

senses.definition: If something that was just mentioned does not happen.
senses.example: We should leave soon, or else we will miss the bus.

senses.definition: To get on a ship or aircraft before a trip.
senses.example: We embarked on the ferry from the small dock.

senses.definition: To begin a new activity or adventure, usually followed by “on.”
senses.example: Our class embarked on a project to map the schoolyard.

senses.definition: To make someone feel awkward, ashamed, or uncomfortable around others.
senses.example: I did not mean to embarrass my friend by pointing out the mix-up.

senses.definition: A design or object that stands for a person, group, place, or idea.
senses.example: Our team used a small owl as its emblem.

senses.definition: To hold someone in your arms, as in a hug.
senses.example: I embraced my aunt when she arrived.

senses.definition: To welcome or gladly start using an idea, change, or opportunity.
senses.example: Our group embraced the chance to make its own rules.

senses.definition: A hug or the act of accepting something warmly.
senses.example: The cousins greeted each other with an embrace.

senses.definition: To come out into view or become known.
senses.example: A frog emerged from beneath the wet log.

senses.definition: To show that a detail, idea, or word is important.
senses.example: I underlined two points to emphasize them.

senses.definition: Someone hired to do work for a person, business, or organization.
senses.example: A museum employee showed us the way to the exhibit.

senses.definition: To fill someone with delight or fascination.
senses.example: The tiny lights enchanted everyone who saw them.

senses.definition: In a story, to put a magic spell on someone or something.
senses.example: The wizard enchanted the cup so that it would sing.

senses.definition: To come across or meet someone or something, often by chance.
senses.example: We encountered a slow-moving turtle on the path.

senses.definition: A meeting or experience with someone or something.
senses.example: Our encounter with the turtle made the walk more memorable.

senses.definition: A book or other collection of articles that explain many subjects or many parts of one subject.
senses.example: We found an article about caves in the encyclopedia.

senses.definition: To get through something difficult without giving up.
senses.example: The team endured a long delay before the race began.

senses.definition: To continue to last over time.
senses.example: The thick stone wall endured for many generations.

senses.definition: Taking an active part or paying close attention.
senses.example: The students were engaged during the mystery story.

senses.definition: Already busy with something.
senses.example: The coach was engaged in a meeting and could not talk yet.

senses.definition: Having agreed to get married.
senses.example: My aunt and her partner are engaged.

senses.definition: To cut words or a design into the surface of a hard material.
senses.example: The artist engraved three small stars in the metal plate.

senses.definition: Pleasant or fun to do or experience.
senses.example: The walk was enjoyable even though the wind was cold.

senses.definition: To make something bigger.
senses.example: I enlarged the photo so we could see the feathers.

senses.definition: To sign up to join a course, school, or group, or to sign someone else up.
senses.example: We enrolled in the Saturday drawing class.

senses.definition: To make certain that something happens or is true.
senses.example: I counted the cups to ensure everyone had one.

senses.definition: To keep someone interested or amused.
senses.example: We entertained the visitors with a puppet show.

senses.definition: Showing plenty of interest or excitement about something.
senses.example: The hikers were enthusiastic about seeing the waterfall.

senses.definition: The act, chance, or right of going into a place.
senses.example: The ticket allowed us entry to the museum.

senses.definition: One piece of information in a list, book, or record.
senses.example: I added a new entry to the garden log.

senses.definition: Something or someone entered in a contest.
senses.example: My drawing was one entry in the school poster contest.

senses.definition: To form a picture in your mind of how something might look or happen.
senses.example: I envisioned the empty lot filled with tulips.

senses.definition: The symbol with two short lines, `=`, that shows the value on one side is the same as the value on the other.
senses.example: Put the equal sign between “2 + 3” and “5.”

senses.definition: In the same amount or to the same degree.
senses.example: We divided the colored pencils equally among the four tables.

senses.definition: To provide the tools, materials, or skills needed for a job or activity.
senses.example: We equipped each team with a ruler and a notebook.

senses.definition: A short trip made to do a particular job, such as dropping off a letter.
senses.example: I ran an errand to pick up the repaired shoes.

senses.definition: So important that it is needed.
senses.example: Water is essential for the plants in our window.

senses.definition: Something needed for a job or task, often used in the plural.
senses.example: Paper and pencils were two of the essentials for our field notes.

senses.definition: To set something up so it can begin to work or last.
senses.example: We established a weekly game club at the library.

senses.definition: To show or find out that something is true.
senses.example: The two receipts established the date of the order.

senses.definition: The usual ways of behaving politely in a particular situation.
senses.example: The coach explained the etiquette of shaking hands after a game.

senses.definition: To avoid or escape something, sometimes by being clever.
senses.example: The rabbit evaded the dog by slipping under a narrow gate.

senses.definition: A careful look at something to decide how well it works or meets a goal.
senses.example: Our evaluation of the ramps showed that the wider one was easier to use.

senses.definition: In the end, after some time has passed.
senses.example: The lost mitten eventually turned up under a bench.

senses.definition: Every person in the group you mean.
senses.example: Everybody in our class picked a book to take home.

senses.definition: In a way that is completely correct, with no difference.
senses.example: Our blocks were exactly the same size.

senses.definition: To describe something as bigger, better, worse, or more important than it really is.
senses.example: If I said the puddle was as wide as the street, I would be exaggerating.

senses.definition: To dig out earth, stone, or other material, often to make a space or uncover what is buried.
senses.example: The workers excavated the spot where the new bridge support would go.

senses.definition: To go beyond an amount, limit, or expectation.
senses.example: The crowd exceeded the number of seats in the room.

senses.definition: Someone or something a rule or usual pattern does not apply to.
senses.example: Everyone wore shoes except the lifeguard, who was the only exception.

senses.definition: To make someone very tired or use up a supply of something.
senses.example: The long walk exhausted our whole group.

senses.definition: Waste gases that come out of an engine.
senses.example: We saw exhaust rise from the back of the bus.

senses.definition: A planned journey with a purpose, such as exploring or making observations.
senses.example: We went on a small expedition to look for animal tracks.

senses.definition: Being near or in contact with something long enough to be affected by it.
senses.example: Exposure to the bright sunlight faded one side of the paper.

senses.definition: Especially beautiful, carefully made, or pleasing.
senses.example: The museum displayed a vase with an exquisite painted pattern.

senses.definition: To take something out from a place or from among other material.
senses.example: We extracted the metal clips from the box of paper scraps.

senses.definition: A part taken from a longer piece of writing or a substance taken from another material.
senses.example: Our teacher read an extract from the new book.

senses.definition: To a very great degree.
senses.example: The bike ride was extremely tiring on that uphill road.

senses.definition: One of the little hairs along the edge of an eyelid.
senses.example: A raindrop clung to my eyelash.

senses.definition: The ability to see.
senses.example: Good light made it easier for my grandfather to read even with poor eyesight.

senses.definition: The front of a building, especially when it is different from the other sides or decorated.
senses.example: The glass facade shone in the afternoon sun.

senses.definition: A way someone appears that hides what they really feel or what is happening.
senses.example: Her confident smile was a facade because she still felt nervous.

senses.definition: A place or set of buildings and equipment made to serve a purpose.
senses.example: The new sports facility has a court and a running track.

senses.definition: A service, room, or piece of equipment that helps people use a place, often in the plural.
senses.example: The campsite facilities include a water tap and two bathrooms.

senses.definition: A group within a larger group that has its own ideas or plans.
senses.example: One faction in the club wanted to build a raised garden instead of planting in pots.

senses.definition: Lacking courage or made nervous easily.
senses.example: In the story, the fainthearted knight paused at the dark gate.

senses.definition: A place where a public fair is held, often with rides, shows, or stands selling food.
senses.example: The whole band met at the fairground before the parade.

senses.definition: A small imaginary being with magical powers, often pictured with wings.
senses.example: In the story, a fairy turned the stones into lanterns.

senses.definition: Loyal and continuing to support someone or something.
senses.example: The faithful dog stayed by her side.

senses.definition: True to the original, without important changes.
senses.example: The sketch was a faithful copy of the mural.

senses.definition: A kind of bird of prey with strong claws and generally long, pointed wings.
senses.example: A falcon circled high above the field.

senses.definition: To become weaker or less steady for a moment, often because of doubt or tiredness.
senses.example: My voice faltered when I lost my place in the speech.

senses.definition: A long time when a large group of people has far too little food.
senses.example: People brought food from nearby regions during the famine.

senses.definition: A long, sharp tooth.
senses.example: The drawing showed two large fangs in the animal’s upper jaw.

senses.definition: The price of a ride on a bus, train, taxi, or other vehicle.
senses.example: I checked the bus fare before we left.

senses.definition: Food of a certain kind, often served at a place or event.
senses.example: The market offered simple fare like bread and warm soup.

senses.definition: To do well or badly in a situation.
senses.example: Our team fared well in the first round.

senses.definition: To close something or attach it firmly in place.
senses.example: I fastened the strap before lifting the bag.

senses.definition: A device with a control that lets water out of a pipe or stops its flow.
senses.example: I turned the faucet off after filling the cup.

senses.definition: Helpful to a plan or likely to bring a good result.
senses.example: The light wind was favorable for launching the kite.

senses.definition: Showing approval or support.
senses.example: Our class gave the new library hours a favorable response.

senses.definition: Showing no fear, even in a difficult or frightening situation.
senses.example: The actor played a fearless explorer.

senses.definition: An answer or comments telling you how something went or how you could improve it.
senses.example: I asked my partner for feedback on my story.

senses.definition: A person, often a man or boy, described in a simple or friendly way.
senses.example: The cheerful fellow at the counter handed us the tickets.

senses.definition: Belonging to the same group or doing the same kind of thing.
senses.example: I asked my fellow students to share their notes.

senses.definition: A soft thick material made from fibers pressed and held together, rather than woven or knitted.
senses.example: We made a puppet out of blue felt.

senses.definition: Past form of “feel,” meaning noticed by touch or had a physical or emotional feeling.
senses.example: I felt proud after reading the whole story aloud.

senses.definition: To take care of yourself without much help, often in the phrase “fend for yourself.”
senses.example: In the book, the young birds soon had to fend for themselves.

senses.definition: To keep something away or stop it from reaching you, often followed by “off.”
senses.example: I used my hat to fend off the little cloud of gnats.

senses.definition: A plant that makes spores rather than flowers and often has large leaves divided into many small parts.
senses.example: A fern grew in the shade beside the steps.

senses.definition: A small animal related to a weasel, with a long body and short legs.
senses.example: The pet ferret hid behind a cardboard box.

senses.definition: To search carefully until something is found, often followed by “out.”
senses.example: We ferreted out three missing puzzle pieces from under the rug.

senses.definition: Able to support plenty of plant growth.
senses.example: The garden’s fertile soil helped the beans grow quickly.

senses.definition: Able to produce young or new living things.
senses.example: The fertile seeds grew into seedlings on the windowsill.

senses.definition: To go and get someone or something and bring them back.
senses.example: I fetched a clean towel for the wet puppy.

senses.definition: A complete failure that causes confusion or embarrassment.
senses.example: Our shadow show was a fiasco when all three cardboard animals fell down.

senses.definition: A tightly curled young leaf of a fern.
senses.example: We spotted tiny fiddleheads beside the path and left them to grow.

senses.definition: To make small restless movements, especially when waiting or trying to sit still.
senses.example: I started to fidget after waiting on the bench for a long time.

senses.definition: A player who tries to catch or stop a ball hit by another player.
senses.example: The fielder grabbed the ball before it rolled to the fence.

senses.definition: Very strong, active, or determined in a way that can seem frightening.
senses.example: A fierce wind bent the trees.

senses.definition: Very intense or difficult to overcome.
senses.example: There was fierce competition to reach the final round.

senses.definition: A soft sweet fruit that can be eaten fresh or dried.
senses.example: I tried a dried fig with my lunch.

senses.definition: Food put inside another food, or material put into an opening.
senses.example: The dumpling had a warm vegetable filling.

senses.definition: Making you feel as though you have eaten enough.
senses.example: The bowl of bean soup was filling.

senses.definition: Putting something into an empty or partly empty space, from the verb “fill.”
senses.example: I was filling my water bottle when the bus arrived.

senses.definition: Very dirty.
senses.example: My shoes were filthy after the walk through the mud.

senses.definition: A kind of small bird, often with a short, strong bill that helps it eat seeds.
senses.example: A finch hopped onto the feeder.

senses.definition: A kind of beetle that can make light in its body, often seen flashing on warm nights.
senses.example: A firefly flashed over the grass.

senses.definition: A person who catches fish for food, a living, or a sport.
senses.example: A fisher watched her line from the edge of the pier.

senses.definition: A North American animal related to weasels, with a long body and a dark coat.
senses.example: The ranger showed us a photo of a fisher climbing a tree.

senses.definition: To shine with quick changes between bright and dim.
senses.example: The lights flickered just before the power went out.

senses.definition: A brief change, movement, or flash.
senses.example: I saw a flicker of light beneath the door.

senses.definition: Thin or weak enough to bend, tear, or break too easily.
senses.example: The flimsy bag tore when I put the books in it.

senses.definition: To grow or do very well.
senses.example: The herbs flourished in the sunny corner.

senses.definition: To wave or hold something up in a bold way so other people notice it.
senses.example: The conductor flourished a small baton before the music began.

senses.definition: A showy extra movement or curved detail added for effect.
senses.example: She signed her name with a flourish.

senses.definition: To move with quick light flaps, like wings or loose paper.
senses.example: The ribbons fluttered in the breeze.

senses.definition: A quick light movement or feeling.
senses.example: I felt a flutter in my stomach before going onstage.

senses.definition: The leaves of a plant or group of plants.
senses.example: The trees’ golden foliage filled the hillside.

senses.definition: A workshop or part of a workshop where someone heats and works metal.
senses.example: The museum guide led us past the old forge.

senses.definition: To shape metal by working it, or to make a connection with effort.
senses.example: The two groups forged a friendship by helping each other.

senses.definition: To make a false copy of something, such as someone’s signature.
senses.example: In the mystery, someone forged the coach’s name on the form.

senses.definition: So powerful or difficult that facing it takes courage or effort.
senses.example: The steep hill looked formidable from the bottom.

senses.definition: A smell, usually a pleasant one.
senses.example: The fragrance of the orange peel filled the room.

senses.definition: Physically weak or easy to break or damage.
senses.example: The frail paper tore when I tried to unfold it.

senses.definition: Very hurried or upset, as if there is not enough time to think calmly.
senses.example: My search became frantic when I heard the bus pulling up.

senses.definition: A small brownish spot on the skin.
senses.example: A freckle on my left thumb looks a little like a circle.

senses.definition: Very cold.
senses.example: We wore several layers in the frigid morning air.

senses.definition: To play and move around in a lively, happy way.
senses.example: The lambs frolicked in the open field.

senses.definition: To make someone feel upset or annoyed because something keeps them from doing what they want.
senses.example: The stack of mismatched lids frustrated me while I searched for the right one.

senses.definition: A soft sweet food often made with sugar, milk, and chocolate.
senses.example: We made a small batch of chocolate fudge.

senses.definition: To present information in a way that hides part of the truth or leaves out exact details.
senses.example: I did not want to fudge the numbers after we measured the room.

senses.definition: To handle something awkwardly, often while trying to get hold of it quickly.
senses.example: I fumbled for the key with my mittens on.

senses.definition: The act of losing hold of a ball during play, especially in football.
senses.example: The other team got the ball after a fumble.

senses.definition: Very angry.
senses.example: My friend was furious when we landed on her carefully built sandcastle by mistake.

senses.definition: Very fast, busy, or strong.
senses.example: The wind began to blow at a furious speed.

senses.definition: A machine or enclosed place that produces heat for warming air or for heating materials.
senses.example: The furnace keeps our house warm in winter.
